mainTopic: Suspicion and trust: how far suspicion spreads, and how a person becomes and stays a חבר.
overview: The גמרא finishes a disagreement about who the unnamed 'חכמים' are: one view says רבי יהודה, the other says רבי מאיר, who holds that suspicion in one matter spreads to the whole תורה. A גר suspected in one matter is treated like a ישראל משומד, but his קידושין still work. A would-be חבר, גר, לוי or כהן who refuses even one matter is not accepted. The גמרא then lays out how a person becomes a חבר: whether he is taught first or accepted first, hands before טהרות, and how long the trial period lasts. There, the גמרא corrects בית הלל's view to thirty days. After a memory list, ברייתות teach who must accept in front of three חברים, including a family and a תלמיד חכם. A story about the son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס shows כהנים guarding their טהרות even from Torah students. The amud ends with how trusted status passes between households, where רבי מאיר holds that people take on the ways of their new home.

steps.title: The first view finishes: the חכמים are רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The first אמורא finishes his view. Someone suspected about שביעית is suspected about מעשר, and the 'חכמים' in the earlier teaching are רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One said: someone suspected about שביעית is] suspected about מעשר. And who are the 'חכמים'? רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the first of two opinions about who the unnamed 'חכמים' are. This opinion says they are רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהודה's area, people treated שביעית very strictly. So a person who breaks שביעית has shown he would surely break מעשר too. Suspicion here moves from the 'stricter' area to the 'lighter' one.

keyTerms.meaning: Suspected; not trusted in a certain area of halacha
Tithes, the required portions taken from produce
The seventh (שמיטה) year and the laws about its produce
And who are the 'Sages'? This asks which named תנא stands behind an unnamed view

phrases.english: is suspected regarding tithe,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence that began just before: 'One says: someone suspected about שביעית...'

phrases.english: and who are the Sages? Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן חֲכָמִים? רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the first opinion of a disagreement that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone suspected about שביעית is suspected about מעשר. The unnamed חכמים are רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The second view: the חכמים are רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The other אמורא reverses the direction. Someone suspected about מעשר is suspected about שביעית, and the 'חכמים' are רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one said: someone suspected about מעשר is suspected about שביעית. And who are the 'חכמים'? רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The second אמורא gives the opposite reading. He says the 'חכמים' are רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, suspicion moves from מעשר to שביעית. It fits רבי מאיר, who holds that a person suspected in one thing is suspected in everything. The next step brings a ברייתא to show that this really is רבי מאיר's position.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one says; this introduces the second side of a disagreement

phrases.english: And one said:

phrases.aramaic: הֶחָשׁוּד עַל הַמַּעֲשֵׂר חָשׁוּד עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית,
phrases.english: one suspected regarding tithe is suspected regarding the Sabbatical Year,
and who are the Sages? Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reading of the same unnamed חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone suspected about מעשר is suspected about שביעית. The unnamed חכמים are רבי מאיר.

steps.title: A ברייתא showing רבי מאיר's view that suspicion spreads
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר holds a חבר suspected in one matter is suspected in the whole תורה. The חכמים disagree and limit the suspicion to that one matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: an עם הארץ who took on the commitments of a חבר, and was then suspected in one matter, is suspected about the whole תורה. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say he is suspected only in that one matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the second view. It shows that רבי מאיר really does believe suspicion in one area spreads to everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, one known failure ruins the person's reliability everywhere. That is why he would say someone suspected about מעשר is also suspected about שביעית. The חכמים of this ברייתא disagree: they keep the suspicion limited to the one area where he was caught.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary person who is not careful about טומאה and מעשרות
The commitments of a חבר: being careful with מעשרות and טהרה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two groups of 'חכמים'. The 'חכמים' inside this ברייתא disagree with רבי מאיר. But the second view in step 2 says the unnamed 'חכמים' of the earlier teaching are רבי מאיר himself.

phrases.english: As it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: עַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוּת,
phrases.english: an am ha'aretz who accepted upon himself the matters of a haver,
and was suspected regarding one matter,
is suspected regarding the entire Torah,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ נֶחְשָׁד אֶלָּא לְאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: he is suspected only regarding that matter alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second view by showing what רבי מאיר holds.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר holds suspicion in one matter spreads to other matters.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about an עם הארץ who became a חבר and was then suspected in one matter.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the general dispute behind the whole discussion: does suspicion stay in its own area, or does it spread to everything?

steps.title: A גר suspected in one matter is like a ישראל משומד
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a גר who was suspected in even one matter is suspected about the whole תורה. He is treated like a ישראל משומד.
steps.simpleTranslation: A גר who accepted the words of the תורה, if he was suspected in even one matter, is suspected about the whole תורה. He is like a ישראל משומד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching about spreading suspicion, this time about a גר. It compares him to a ישראל משומד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a גר, the suspicion spreads to the whole תורה. But notice the comparison: he is called a sinning Jew, not a non-Jew. The next step explains what difference this makes.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jew who regularly breaks the מצוות

phrases.english: A convert who accepted upon himself the words of Torah,
even if he was suspected regarding one matter,
he is suspected regarding the entire Torah,
and he is like a Jewish transgressor.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַגֵּר שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ברייתא about how far suspicion spreads, this time for a גר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר suspected in one matter is suspected about the whole תורה and is like a ישראל משומד.

steps.title: What being 'like a משומד' changes: his קידושין still work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the practical difference of calling him 'like a ישראל משומד'. If he does קידושין, they are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The practical difference: if he betroths a woman, his קידושין are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא compared the גר to a sinning Jew. Even though he is suspected about everything, he is still Jewish, so his marriage takes effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that a גר who isn't keeping the מצוות loses his conversion. The comparison to a משומד shows he does not: he stays a Jew, just an untrusted one. That is why his קידושין count.

keyTerms.meaning: Halachic betrothal, the first stage of marriage

steps.whatToRemember: A גר who is suspected in one matter loses his trustworthiness about the whole תורה, but he does not lose his Jewish status. His קידושין are valid.

phrases.english: The practical difference is
that if he betroths, his betrothal is a valid betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical result of the phrase 'like a ישראל משומד' in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A suspected גר keeps his Jewish status, so his קידושין are valid.

steps.title: Accepting everything except one matter is not accepted
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that someone who wants to become a חבר, or a non-Jew who wants to convert, but refuses one matter, is not accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: one who comes to accept the commitments of a חבר except for one matter is not accepted. A non-Jew who comes to accept the תורה except for one matter is not accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a related teaching about the moment of acceptance. A partial commitment is not enough, both for a חבר and for a גר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the topic was someone who accepted everything and was later suspected. Now it is someone who openly refuses one matter from the start. The ruling is that his commitment does not count at all, not even for the parts he agrees to.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who comes to accept the matters of a haver,
except for one matter,
we do not accept him.
A gentile who comes to accept the words of Torah,
except for one matter,
we do not accept him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from suspicion after acceptance to an incomplete acceptance at the start.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A would-be חבר or גר who refuses even one matter is not accepted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule for גירות: the convert must accept the whole תורה, with nothing left out.

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: even one rabbinic detail
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה extends the rule. Refusing even one small detail of דברי סופרים is enough to be turned away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: even one detail of the words of the סופרים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה adds a stronger version of the previous rule. Even refusing one fine point of rabbinic law means the person is not accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the 'one matter' must be a full תורה law. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says even a small rabbinic detail counts. Accepting the תורה includes accepting the words of the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Rabbinic laws, the words of the Sages

steps.whatToRemember: A חבר or גר must accept everything. Refusing even one matter, and according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה even one small rabbinic detail, means he is not accepted.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
even one detail of the words of the scribes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the ברייתא's rule to include even small rabbinic details.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Refusing even one detail of דברי סופרים blocks acceptance.

steps.title: A Levite or priest who rejects one detail is not accepted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא extends the rule. A בן לוי or כהן who accepts all the rules of his role except one is not accepted, as learned from a פסוק about the sons of אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the same way, a בן לוי who comes to take on the duties of a לוי, or a כהן who comes to take on the duties of כהונה, but leaves out one thing, is not accepted. The פסוק says 'He who offers the blood of the peace offerings', which teaches that a כהן who does not agree to the whole עבודה given to the sons of אהרן has no share in כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 6 continues. It applies the 'refusing even one thing' rule to a בן לוי and a כהן too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the rule covered a חבר and a גר. Now it is applied to the special duties of לויים and כהנים, and this time a פסוק is given as the source. The idea is that the עבודה is one whole package: a כהן who rejects any part of it loses his share in כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: The duties and rules of a לוי
Priesthood: the role and duties of a כהן
Handed over to the sons of אהרן

phrases.english: And similarly, a Levite who comes
to accept the duties of a Levite,
and a priest who comes to accept the duties of priesthood,
except for one matter —
we do not accept him,
as it says: "He who offers the blood of the peace offerings, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:33. The end of the פסוק says that this כהן gets a portion.

phrases.english: the service that is handed over to the sons of Aaron:
any priest who does not agree to it —
has no share in the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן בֶּן לֵוִי שֶׁבָּא לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי לְוִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and applies the 'all or nothing' rule to a לוי and a כהן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לוי or כהן who accepts every duty of his role except one is not accepted. A כהן who denies any part of the עבודה has no share in כהונה.

steps.title: Teach first or accept first: it depends on his private behavior
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: if we have seen a would-be חבר keeping the rules privately at home, we accept him and then teach him. If not, we teach him first and accept him afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if someone comes to take on the ways of a חבר, and we have seen him keep them quietly in his own home, we accept him first and teach him the details afterward. If we have not seen this, we teach him first and accept him afterward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the order of becoming a חבר: is he accepted first or taught first?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is whether he already lives this way in private. If he has a proven track record, he can be accepted right away and learn the fine points later. If not, he must first learn the rules, and only then is he accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: The rules and commitments of being a חבר
Privately, modestly, when no one is watching

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
one who comes to accept the ways of a ḥaver,
if we saw that he practices them privately
inside his home —
we accept him,
and afterward we teach him.
And if not — we teach him,
and afterward we accept him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַבָּא לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whether a חבר is accepted at all to the order of how he is accepted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he already keeps the rules privately, accept him and then teach him. Otherwise teach him first, then accept him.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחי: always accept him first
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי disagrees and says we always accept him first, and he keeps learning as he goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: either way we accept him, and he keeps learning in the normal way as he goes along.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion inside the same ברייתא disagrees with the first view in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view makes the order depend on his private behavior. רבי שמעון בן יוחי removes that condition: he is always accepted right away. Learning the details is simply part of the ongoing life of a חבר.

keyTerms.meaning: In his usual way, gradually as he goes along

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ,
phrases.english: either way, we accept him,
and he keeps learning in his usual way as he goes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He is always accepted first, whatever his past, and learns the details over time.

steps.title: First the hands, then full purity
steps.stepSummary: Acceptance comes in stages: first the purity of the hands (כנפים), then טהרות in general. Taking on only hands is allowed, but taking on טהרות without hands is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: first we accept him for hands, and afterward for טהרות. If he says 'I am only taking on hands,' we accept him. But if he takes on טהרות and not hands, he is not accepted even for טהרות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא explains the stages of becoming a חבר: the hands come first, then purity in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing the hands is the easy, basic step, so it comes first and can be accepted on its own. Skipping it while claiming the harder level of טהרות does not work. It is the 'refusing one thing' idea again: whoever rejects the basic part is not trusted for the bigger part.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'wings'; here it means the hands and keeping them pure
Purity rules in general, handling food in purity
He accepted, he took upon himself

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: we accept him for hands,
phrases.notes: כנפים literally means 'wings', but here it refers to the hands, meaning he washes them before touching pure food.

phrases.english: and afterward we accept him for purity in general,
and if he says: "I am accepting only hands" —
we accept him.
If he accepted purity but did not accept hands —
he has not been accepted even for purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מְקַבְּלִין לִכְנָפַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues describing how a חבר is accepted, now looking at the stages of commitment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hands may be taken on alone, but טהרות cannot be taken on without hands.

steps.title: How long until he is accepted
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks how long the trial period lasts. בית שמאי: thirty days for liquids, twelve months for clothing. בית הלל: twelve months for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: how long until he is accepted? בית שמאי say: for liquids, thirty days; for clothing, twelve months. בית הלל say: for both, twelve months.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ברייתא asks how long a would-be חבר must keep the rules before he is trusted, and gives a disagreement between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי make the time depend on the area: liquids need only thirty days, while clothing needs a full year. בית הלל do not divide them. For both, he needs twelve months before he is fully accepted.
steps.whatToRemember: Becoming a חבר means taking on everything (no exceptions), it happens in stages (hands before טהרות), and it needs a trial period. As written here, בית הלל say twelve months for both, but steps 13-14 correct this: בית הלל say thirty days for both.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַד כַּמָּה מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ?
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: how long until we accept him?
Beit Shammai say:
for liquids — thirty days,
for clothing — twelve months.
And Beit Hillel say:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה — לִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: both this and that — twelve months.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַד כַּמָּה מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the stages of acceptance, gives the length of the trial period.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: liquids need thirty days and clothing twelve months. בית הלל: both need twelve months.

steps.title: This would make בית שמאי more lenient than בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא as written gives an unusual case where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this would be one of the leniencies of בית שמאי and the stringencies of בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from Step 12. As written, בית הלל would be stricter than בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 12, בית שמאי require only thirty days for liquids, but בית הלל require twelve months. That makes בית הלל stricter on liquids, which is a rare pattern. Such cases are normally listed as a known group, and this one is not among them.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a problem that follows from what was just said)
From the leniencies of בית שמאי
From the stringencies of בית הלל

steps.confusionAlert: Usually בית שמאי are the strict ones and בית הלל the lenient ones. That is exactly why this reading bothers the גמרא.

phrases.english: If so,
this would be one of the leniencies of בית שמאי
and the stringencies of בית הלל,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, הָוֵה לֵיהּ מִקּוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּמֵחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא quoted in Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's version of בית הלל's view (twelve months for both liquids and clothing)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It would create a case of בית שמאי being lenient and בית הלל strict that is not on the known list of such cases.

steps.title: Correcting בית הלל to thirty days for both
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording so that בית הלל say thirty days for both liquids and clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, בית הלל say: both this and that are thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem by correcting the ברייתא's wording of בית הלל's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now בית הלל require only thirty days for clothing too, where בית שמאי required twelve months. This makes בית הלל the more lenient side, which is the usual pattern. The problem from Step 13 disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one

steps.whatToRemember: Final version: בית שמאי say thirty days for liquids and twelve months for clothing. בית הלל say thirty days for both.

phrases.english: Rather, בית הלל say:
Both this and that are thirty days.
phrases.notes: "This and that" means the liquids and the clothing from Step 12.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה לִשְׁלשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית הלל require twelve months for both liquids and clothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל require thirty days for both, which makes them more lenient than בית שמאי.

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming topics
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a list of key words to help remember the order of the topics that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: חבר, student, תכלת, tax, returned, collector, by himself.)
steps.whatsHappening: This is a transition line. The גמרא is not teaching a law here; it is setting up a memory list for the upcoming sections.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to one coming topic. For example, "חבר" is the next ברייתא about accepting in front of three, and "student" is the one about the תלמיד חכם. The list just helps a learner keep the order straight.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid listing upcoming topics

phrases.english: (Memory aid: חבר, student,
תכלת, tax, returned,
collector, by himself).

steps.triggerLanguage: סִימָן: חָבֵר, תַּלְמִיד, תְּכֵלֶת, מֶכֶס, חָזַר, גַּבַּאי, בְּעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Marks a shift to a new set of topics
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling; it only lists the upcoming topics.

steps.title: Accepting חבר status in front of three חברים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a new חבר must accept in front of three חברים, but his children and household do not need to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: one who comes to accept the rules of being a חבר must accept them in front of three חברים. His children and household members do not need to accept in front of three חברים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about how a person formally becomes a חבר: he must accept in front of three חברים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The acceptance must be public, in front of three. The ברייתא adds that this is not required of his children and household. Their status comes along with his.

keyTerms.meaning: The rules of being a חבר

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who comes to accept the rules of being a חבר
must accept them in front of three חברים,
but his children and household members

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָן צְרִיכִין לְקַבֵּל בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲבֵירִים.
phrases.english: do not need to accept in front of three חברים.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַבָּא לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First topic of the memory aid ("חבר")
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Acceptance must be in front of three חברים, but the חבר's children and household are exempt from this.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: children also need three
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that the children and household must also accept in front of three, because a son is not like his father who accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: even his children and household members must accept in front of three חברים, because a חבר who accepted is not like the son of a חבר who accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with the first opinion. He says the family members also need their own acceptance in front of three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason is that the father accepted personally and publicly. The son only follows his father. Following a father's commitment is weaker than making one yourself, so the son needs his own formal acceptance.

phrases.english: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:
Even his children and household members
must accept in front of three חברים,
because a חבר who accepted is not similar
to the son of a חבר who accepted.
phrases.notes: The father accepted himself in front of three. The son's commitment comes only through his father.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אַף בָּנָיו וּבְנֵי בֵיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the exemption for children in Step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Children and household members also need to accept in front of three חברים.

steps.title: Even a תלמיד חכם needs three, but an elder in the ישיבה does not
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says even a תלמיד חכם must accept in front of three, but an elder who sits in the ישיבה is exempt because he already accepted when he took his seat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: one who comes to accept the rules of being a חבר must accept in front of three חברים, and even a תלמיד חכם must. An elder who sits in the ישיבה does not need to accept in front of three, since he already accepted from the time he sat.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ברייתא applies the rule of three to scholars. A regular תלמיד חכם still needs it, but a זקן sitting in the ישיבה does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being learned is not enough by itself, so a תלמיד חכם still needs a formal acceptance. A זקן who sits in the ישיבה is different. Taking that seat already counts as accepting the rules.

keyTerms.meaning: An elder who sits in the ישיבה

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who comes to accept the rules of being a חבר
must accept in front of three חברים,
and even a תלמיד חכם
must accept in front of three חברים.
An elder who sits in the ישיבה

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְקַבֵּל בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲבֵירִים,
phrases.english: does not need to accept in front of three חברים,
since he already accepted it upon himself from the time he sat.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַבָּא לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוּת — צָרִיךְ לְקַבֵּל בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲבֵירִים, וַאֲפִילּוּ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second topic of the memory aid ("student"); applies the rule of three to scholars
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם must accept in front of three; an elder sitting in the ישיבה is exempt because his sitting already counts as acceptance.

steps.title: אבא שאול: a תלמיד חכם is exempt and others accept before him
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול holds that even a תלמיד חכם does not need to accept in front of three, and others may even accept in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: even a תלמיד חכם does not need to accept in front of three חברים. Not only that, but others may accept in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא שאול disagrees with the ברייתא. He gives the regular תלמיד חכם the same exemption as the elder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אבא שאול, being a Torah scholar already shows a full commitment to the rules. He goes further: the תלמיד חכם is trusted enough that new people may make their acceptance in front of him.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but even
They accept in front of him

steps.whatToRemember: Who needs three חברים: a regular person always does. For his children, the first opinion says no and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says yes. For a תלמיד חכם, the first opinion says yes and אבא שאול says no. An elder sitting in the ישיבה is exempt.

phrases.english: אבא שאול says:
Even a תלמיד חכם

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְקַבֵּל בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲבֵירִים,
phrases.english: does not need to accept in front of three חברים,
and not only that, but
others may accept in front of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: אַף תַּלְמִיד חָכָם אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְקַבֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the first opinion of Step 18 about a תלמיד חכם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם is exempt from accepting in front of three, and others may accept in front of him.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן dates the ruling to the son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the ruling that even a תלמיד חכם must accept in front of three was taught in the days of the son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: This teaching was taught in the days of the son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן tells us when the strict ruling from the ברייתא in step 18 was taught. This sets up the story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 said even a תלמיד חכם must accept in front of three, and אבא שאול disagreed. רבי יוחנן ties the strict view to a particular time and person. The story that follows will show what that strictness looked like in practice.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:

phrases.aramaic: בִּימֵי בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס
phrases.english: In the days of the son of Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus
this teaching was taught.
phrases.notes: "This teaching" means the ruling from step 18, that even a תלמיד חכם must accept in front of three.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בִּימֵי בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס נִשְׁנֵית מִשְׁנָה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the historical setting of the strict ruling in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling that even a תלמיד חכם must accept in front of three comes from the era of the son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.

steps.title: The students sent to the son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס are not trusted with pure items
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי had a question about טהרות and sent students to ask. The son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס was carrying pure items, so he had his own students sit next to the visitors before he went to look into the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי were unsure about a matter of purity. The חכמים sent students to the son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס and told them: go tell him to look into it. They found him carrying pure items. He seated חכמים of his own next to them, and he stood to look into the question.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing how strictly this כהן guarded his pure items, even from visiting Torah students.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He did not let the visiting students stay alone near his טהרות. He seated his own trusted students beside them to watch the items. This treated the visitors as if they could not be trusted with purity, which is what upsets רבי יהודה in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: items that must be kept ritually pure

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei
were unsure about a matter of purity,
the Sages sent [students] to

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס,
phrases.english: the son of Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus,
[saying:] Go and tell him to look into it.
They found him carrying pure items,
he seated Sages of his own next to them,
and he stood to look into the question.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אִיסְתַּפַּק לְהוּ מִילְּתָא בִּטְהָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells the story that shows the era רבי יוחנן described.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס did not trust visiting students with his טהרות.

steps.title: רבי יהודה complains that father and son degrade Torah scholars
steps.stepSummary: When the students report back, רבי יהודה is upset. He says the father used to degrade תלמידי חכמים, and now the son does the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came and told רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה said to them: This one's father degraded Torah scholars, and he too degrades Torah scholars!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה objects to how the students were treated. He calls it an insult to Torah scholars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view, not trusting a תלמיד חכם with purity is disrespectful. He says the father, רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, behaved the same way. This attack sets up רבי יוסי's defense in the next step.

phrases.english: They came and told
Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei,
Rabbi Yehuda said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אָבִיו שֶׁל זֶה בִּיזָּה תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים,
phrases.english: This one's father degraded Torah scholars,
and he too degrades Torah scholars!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָבִיו שֶׁל זֶה בִּיזָּה תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the treatment described in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conduct of the son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Refusing to trust תלמידי חכמים with purity is an insult to them.

steps.title: רבי יוסי explains the כהנים' extra strictness after the חורבן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי defends the son: it was not an insult. Since the בית המקדש was destroyed, כהנים took on a higher standard and do not hand pure items to just anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to him: Let the honor of the elder stay in its place. Rather, from the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, the כהנים took on a higher standard for themselves, that they do not hand pure items to just anyone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי answers רבי יהודה's complaint. He explains that the son was following a special custom of כהנים, not insulting anyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says we should respect the elder and not accuse him. The behavior came from an extra strictness כהנים took on, which applies to everyone and is not aimed at Torah scholars. So the son acted properly as a כהן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to him:
Let the honor of the elder stay in its place,
rather, from the day the Temple was destroyed
the כהנים took on a higher standard for themselves,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין מוֹסְרִין אֶת הַטְּהָרוֹת לְכׇל אָדָם.
phrases.english: that they do not hand pure items to just anyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּבוֹד זָקֵן יְהֵא מוּנָּח בִּמְקוֹמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהודה's complaint from step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the behavior as a general custom of כהנים, not an insult.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The son was showing disrespect to תלמידי חכמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was keeping the extra strictness כהנים adopted after the חורבן, which applies to everyone.
steps.whatToRemember: The son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס did not trust even Torah students with his טהרות, and רבי יוסי explains this as a strict custom of כהנים after the חורבן, not an insult.

steps.title: A dead חבר's family and a תכלת shop keep their trusted status
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when a חבר dies, his wife, children and household stay trusted until there is reason to suspect them. A courtyard that sells תכלת also stays trusted until it is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: A חבר who died, his wife, children and household keep their presumed status until they are suspected. And likewise a courtyard where they sell תכלת keeps its presumed status until it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about how long a trusted status lasts. It gives two examples: a חבר's family and a תכלת shop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The family got their trusted status through the חבר. Even after he dies, they keep it automatically and do not need to accept again. The same idea applies to a place known for selling proper תכלת: we keep trusting it until something goes wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: the blue dye used for ציצית

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A חבר who died —
his wife, his children and his household
keep their presumed status, until they are suspected.
And likewise, a courtyard in which they sell תכלת —
keeps its presumed status, until it is disqualified.
phrases.notes: We keep assuming the תכלת sold there is proper until the place shows it can't be trusted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חָבֵר שֶׁמֵּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the story to the laws of a חבר's household, which step 16 discussed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dead חבר's family, and a courtyard selling תכלת, stay trusted until there is a reason to suspect them.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a trusted status, once set up, stays in place until there is a real reason to doubt it.

steps.title: Moving into a חבר's home requires accepting the commitments
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the wife, daughter or slave of an עם הארץ who joins a חבר's household must formally accept the commitments of a חבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: a woman who was married to an עם הארץ and then marries a חבר, a daughter of an עם הארץ who marries a חבר, and a slave of an עם הארץ who is sold to a חבר must all accept the commitments of a חבר from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about people who move from an עם הארץ's household into a חבר's household. It rules that they must formally commit to the standards of a חבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These people grew up or lived among people who were not careful about the laws of purity and מעשרות. So we cannot assume they behave like a חבר just because they joined a חבר's home. They need to accept these commitments formally before they are trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is not careful about purity and מעשרות
A person who has formally committed to keep purity and מעשרות carefully
The commitments a person takes on to become a חבר
From the start, as a fresh commitment

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The wife of an am ha'aretz who married a chaver,
and likewise the daughter of an am ha'aretz
who married a chaver,
and likewise the slave of an am ha'aretz
who was sold to a chaver
all of them need to accept
the commitments of a chaver from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵשֶׁת עַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְחָבֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of step 24, which dealt with a חבר's household and who stays trusted, by now discussing people who move between households.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People who move from an עם הארץ's household into a חבר's household must formally accept the commitments of a חבר.

steps.title: Moving from a חבר's home does not require accepting them again
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the wife, daughter or slave of a חבר who moves into an עם הארץ's household does not need to accept the commitments again.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a woman who was married to a חבר and then marries an עם הארץ, a daughter of a חבר who marries an עם הארץ, and a slave of a חבר who is sold to an עם הארץ do not need to accept the commitments of a חבר from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the opposite case: people moving out of a חבר's home into an עם הארץ's home. It rules that they do not need a fresh commitment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These people already lived the life of a חבר, so their careful habits are assumed to stay with them. Moving into an עם הארץ's home does not cancel the trust they already have. This is the opinion of the תנא קמא, the first, unnamed opinion in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: But; this signals the contrasting case

phrases.english: But the wife of a chaver
who married an am ha'aretz,
and likewise the daughter of a chaver
who married an am ha'aretz,
and likewise the slave of a chaver
who was sold to an am ha'aretz
do not need to accept
the commitments of a chaver from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אֵשֶׁת חָבֵר שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְעַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse case of step 25, with the opposite ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, people who move from a חבר's household into an עם הארץ's household keep their trust without a new commitment.

steps.title: רבי מאיר requires a new commitment in the reverse case too
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר disagrees and says that even those moving from a חבר's home into an עם הארץ's home must accept the commitments from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: they too must take on the commitments of a חבר from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר argues with the second half of the ברייתא. He says the people in step 26 also need a fresh commitment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי מאיר's view, a person's past as part of a חבר's home is not enough once they join an עם הארץ's home. The new household can change how careful they are, so their old trust does not carry over automatically.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
They too need to accept upon themselves
phrases.notes: "They" means the people in the second case: those who moved from a חבר's home to an עם הארץ's home.

phrases.english: the commitments of a chaver from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אַף הֵן צְרִיכִין לְקַבֵּל עֲלֵיהֶן דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוּת לְכַתְּחִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling of the תנא קמא in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even people who move from a חבר's household into an עם הארץ's household must accept the commitments of a חבר again.
steps.whyThisMatters: The disagreement turns on whether a person's habits come from their past or from the household they now live in.

steps.title: A story showing that a wife follows her current husband's ways
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר tells, in רבי מאיר's name, of a woman who tied תפילין for her חבר husband and later tied tax collector's seals for her עם הארץ husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said in the name of רבי מאיר: there was a woman who married a חבר and would tie his תפילין on his hand. Later she married an עם הארץ and would tie tax collector's seals on his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: A story is brought to support רבי מאיר. It shows that the same woman fully took on the ways of whichever husband she was married to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When she was with the חבר, she helped him with a מצוה. When she was with the עם הארץ, she helped him with his tax collector's job. This proves that a person's behavior follows their new household, which is why רבי מאיר does not let old trust carry over.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא says a person from a חבר's household keeps their trust after moving. רבי מאיר says they must accept the commitments again, because people take on the ways of their new home, as the woman in the story did.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Meir:
There was an incident with a certain woman
who married a chaver

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיְתָה קוֹמַעַת לוֹ תְּפִילִּין עַל יָדוֹ,
phrases.english: and she would tie tefillin on his hand for him,
She married an am ha'aretz

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיְתָה קוֹשֶׁרֶת לוֹ קִשְׁרֵי מוֹכֵס עַל יָדוֹ.
phrases.english: and she would tie tax collector's seals on his hand for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאִשָּׁה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי מאיר's opinion in step 27 with a real-life story.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's ruling that someone leaving a חבר's household must accept the commitments again
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story, told in רבי מאיר's name, of a woman whose behavior completely changed to match each husband
